schemes.official_name: Community-Based Learning and Research (CBLR) course designation
schemes.description: Curricular designation for courses across departments that must involve collaboration with community partners on a social challenge, include in-depth community experience and reflection, and create products shared with the partner and/or public. Group work, project form and partner type vary by course; individual child courses are not enumerated here other than those assessed separately.
schemes.admin_host: The College (College Curriculum Council) / Swearer Center
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: Courses across many departments; eligibility is set by each course (prerequisites/enrolment caps may apply).
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: Per-course; Brown pages do not state a general student eligibility rule.
schemes.credit_assessment: Regular course credit (per course); not stated on the pages fetched
schemes.project_evidence: Designation criterion: 'Create products or outcomes that are shared with the community partner and/or broader public' [1], but the form/scale of project differs per course and no single bounded project brief is evidenced for the designation as a whole.
schemes.group_evidence: Designation criteria do not require teamwork; individual courses cited by search summary (CS 1951I teams, ENVS 1555 groups, POLS 1820X case studies) are group-based in places but not verified course-by-course [2].
schemes.employer_evidence: Designation requires 'collaboration with one or more community partners to investigate an important social challenge or problem' and products shared with the partner [1].
schemes.partner_role: Community partner collaborates on the problem and receives outputs; type of partner varies (nonprofits, public bodies).
schemes.named_partners: USAID mentioned for POLS 1820X case studies (search summary, undated) [2]
schemes.deliverable: Products/outcomes shared with community partner and/or public (varies)
schemes.latest_evidenced_year: Fall 2026 (legacy row: Fall 2026 catalogue confirmed; not independently re-verified this session)
schemes.unresolved: Because group working is not shown for the designation as a whole, this is an umbrella; the legacy 'Fall 2026 catalogue' claim was not re-verified (Courses@Brown not fetched). Per-course group/partner evidence needed.

schemes.description: Application-only studio course in which small teams of upper-level computer science undergraduates design, build and test technical projects (e.g. web portals, apps, browser extension) for and with non-profit/social-impact partner organisations, who supply project mentors.
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: Undergraduates with CS 32/33/132 prerequisites (course page, Spring 2023); counts toward CS Engaged Scholars / Engaged Scholarship certificate
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: Application only; enrolment cap; prerequisites CS 32, 33 or 132 (Spring 2023 page)
schemes.project_evidence: 'Students will work in a studio environment to iteratively design, build, and test technical projects' with social change organisations [1]; example outputs (web portal, Chrome extension, Smart Cart app) [2].
schemes.group_evidence: Teams of 3-4 students (search summary, tied to CS1951I course pages) [2]; fetched page says 'small teams' without a number [1].
schemes.employer_evidence: Teams 'work directly with project mentors from non-profits and social impact ventures' [2]; Spring 2023 partners named on course page: The Peace Lab, Student Clinic for Immigrant Justice, Center for Health and Justice Transformation, iCareForYou [1]. Note: Student Clinic for Immigrant Justice is a student-run clinic, possibly university-affiliated; others external.
schemes.partner_role: Provides project mentors and the problem; receives built product
schemes.named_partners: The Peace Lab, Student Clinic for Immigrant Justice, Center for Health and Justice Transformation, iCareForYou (Spring 2023)
schemes.unresolved: No 2025/26 or 2026/27 evidence found (course page shows Spring 2023); whether the course is CBLR-designated not verified.

schemes.official_name: Master of Science in Data Science practicum / capstone (DATA 2050)
schemes.description: Required semester-long team capstone in the Data Science master's: students work in small teams on a data science project sourced from Brown units (departments, labs, researchers) and from external entities (companies, nonprofits). DSI industry page states master's students complete a practicum project with an external company.
schemes.delivery_format: Team project overseen by faculty from core departments
schemes.project_evidence: Course page: 'hands-on thesis project that entails an in-depth study of a current problem in data science'; DSI examples of partner projects (risk model for Citizens Bank etc.) [1][2].
schemes.group_evidence: Search summary says capstone teams usually have 3-4 members [3], but the fetched DATA 2050 page (Fall 2022) does not mention teams, and the DSI page does not state team size.
schemes.employer_evidence: DSI page: master's students must complete a practicum with an external company; named projects with Citizens Bank, Brown Health (internal), FLY Initiative, PerformaMatch [2]. But search summary says projects come from Brown entities as well as external ones [3], and the DATA 2050 page says collaboration with 'an additional faculty member, postdoc, or industry partner' is possible [1], so external coverage is not shown to be standard.
schemes.named_partners: Citizens Bank, Brown Health (internal), Financial Youth Literacy (FLY) Initiative, PerformaMatch (DSI page, undated)
schemes.latest_evidenced_year: Fall 2022 (course page); DSI page mentions 2026 event but no dated cohort
schemes.unresolved: Team size, mandatory external share, and current-year delivery; page names conflict (DSI 'practicum with external company' vs course page 'may collaborate').

profile_md: Brown's open curriculum has no institution-wide compulsory employer project. Found: (1) the CBLR course designation, where designated courses must involve community partners and produce outputs shared with them (group work not required, so umbrella); (2) CS for Social Change (CSCI 1951I), an application-only studio in which teams of 3-4 build products with non-profit partners (evidence from Spring 2023); (3) the Data Science master's practicum, partly with external companies but mixed with internal Brown projects; (4) CEDEC, a Swearer-hosted programme matching supervised student teams to Rhode Island nonprofits/public bodies (2025 launch). Review completed in reduced-depth mode. Internal campus units appear as partners in CEDEC and the DSI capstone and are not counted as external. Current-year delivery is poorly evidenced beyond the legacy Fall 2026 CBLR claim.
gaps: Only about 12 searches/fetches (reduced depth). Current (2025/26+) delivery not verified for S2-S4; per-course CBLR group/partner evidence; ENVS 1555 and other CBLR courses unverified; further departmental capstones likely exist.
